title: uncaughtExceptionMonitor shows a synchronous 15-second PowerShell modal, even for exceptions the app may recover from, and reports runtime crashes as startup failures
test: tests/startupFailureReporter.test.js, run against the real lib/startupRuntime.js in a child process: 'an uncaught exception that an uncaughtException listener handles logs a line but shows no dialog' and 'exit code 0 shows no dialog, also after a handled exception' (both failed before the fix), 'a fatal uncaught exception still exits non-zero and shows one dialog that does not claim a startup failure' (failed before), and the passing-before regression guards 'a recovering listener that exits 1 after logging, as server.js does, shows exactly one dialog', 'a non-zero exit without any exception shows one dialog with the exit code', 'off Windows nothing is shown, but the exception is still logged and the exit code is unchanged'; plus unit tests of installFailureReporter with a fake EventEmitter and an injected notifier (no notify for a handled exception, exactly one for a non-zero exit, none for exit code 0 or off Windows), of formatFailureMessage and createDialogNotifier, a real-process test that a fatal exception still emits 'exit' with a non-zero code and the notifier runs once from exit, and a packaging test
proof: The unchanged lib/startupRuntime.js was run in a child process (node -r preload -r lib/startupRuntime.js scenario.js) with a preload that sets process.platform to 'win32' and replaces child_process.execFileSync with a recorder, so no real PowerShell dialog opens. With an 'uncaughtException' listener that swallows a thrown error and the process then exiting 0, the recorder saw one powershell.exe Popup call, text 'Nextra could not start correctly.' plus the stack, title 'Nextra startup failed' (the monitor called showFailureDialog; in the real app that is a 15 s synchronous execFileSync that freezes the event loop). A fatal uncaught exception produced the same 'could not start correctly' wording although the process may have run for hours. 3 of 6 child-process tests failed for those reasons (output: .arbitra/dev-notes/results/TASK-032-before.txt). After the fix the monitor in lib/startupFailureReporter.js (installFailureReporter(processLike, { notify, platform, log, getFallbackText })) only writes the log line synchronously and remembers the formatted error; the exit handler writes 'process exit code', and for a non-zero code on win32 calls notify once with { code, summary } where summary is the remembered error, else the last stderr lines, else empty. The dialog text is 'Nextra stopped unexpectedly (exit code N).' plus the error and 'Startup log: <latest path>', the Popup title is 'Nextra stopped'. No startup-complete signal reaches lib/startupRuntime.js (server.js keeps serviceReady to itself and may not change), so the wording does not claim a startup failure (section-189067a43c5f50160f1b8635/Q-004 default). Exit codes are unchanged (the child tests assert 1 and 3). 19 tests pass; the full suite passes. The packaged build needs no package-app.js change: scripts/package-app.js copies 'lib' as a directory and hashes it into the build identifier, and a test pins that. The real packager was not run.
